How much should I budget for carpet installation in North Bend, WA?

Grade decides more than square footage here. A typical North Bend project runs $2,000–$4,500, and a 1,200 sq ft main floor with its staircase — the common order in Si View and Forster Woods — usually lands at $5,500–$8,500. Per square foot that's $4 to $7 installed, and the figure already includes labor, carpet, pad, new tack strip and hauling the old stuff out. You set the grade yourself, off samples spread in your own rooms.
Does the mobile carpet showroom really come out to North Bend?

North Bend sits on the regular route for the mobile showroom, not at the far edge of it. Bohdan pulls up with 20+ carpet samples and pad in all three grades, sets them on the floors they'd replace, and lets you judge color in valley light rather than under store fluorescents. Rooms and stairs get measured the same visit, the written price stays with you, and none of it costs a thing.
What does carpet stretching cost in North Bend?

A power stretcher hooks the carpet and hauls the ripples, waves and bunched spots back out flat — for roughly a fifth of what pulling it all out and starting fresh would cost. Around North Bend that work starts at $99 per room. Worth doing as long as the carpet itself has life left in it and you aren't sick of the color.
How much do carpeted stairs cost in North Bend?

Stair carpet starts at $18 per step, installed waterfall style or wrapped cap-and-band. Landings and pie-shaped winders — common in the valley's two-story floor plans — are measured and written into the quote at the visit rather than billed as an extra afterward.
How long does the install actually take?

One day handles most North Bend homes. Three or four rooms plus a staircase is a comfortable single day for the crew; a whole house with stairs and heavy furniture can spill into a second. Either way, the schedule goes on your written quote so you can plan around it.
Will the installers move my furniture?

Yes. Beds, dressers, couches and tables are included on most jobs, and everything goes back where it stood once the carpet is in. We ask you to clear the small things ahead of time — closet floors, electronics, breakables, and anything you'd rather carry yourself.
Stretch my carpet, or replace it?

Three things decide it: pile, backing, color. Pile that still springs back, a solid backing, and a color you can live with add up to a $99-per-room stretch rather than a new floor. Crushed traffic lanes, seams pulling open, backing turning to powder, or odor that outlasted a professional cleaning point the other way. Si View bungalows and Forster Woods two-stories land on both sides of that line, so we look before quoting.
Which North Bend neighborhoods do you cover?

All of them — downtown North Bend, Si View, Forster Woods, Tanner, Riverbend, Cedar Falls, Wilderness Rim, Edgewick, Maloney Grove and Sallal Prairie — plus Snoqualmie, Snoqualmie Ridge, Fall City, Preston and up toward Snoqualmie Pass. Farther out, say along the Middle Fork road? Ask when you book; the van usually still comes.
What carpet is best for muddy dogs?

Start underneath. Odor that never leaves starts in the subfloor, not in the carpet on top of it, so the first defense is a moisture-barrier pad — an upgrade that runs $0.65 per square foot and up. Over that goes solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing: pigment locked inside the fiber, so diluted bleach lifts a stain without lifting the color. Around here, where the dog comes back from Little Si caked to the knees, that pairing earns its price.
What's the warranty on the installation work?

Two separate warranties, and both get written onto your quote. The mill's covers the carpet itself — wear and stain, 10 to 25 years depending on the grade you buy. Ours covers the labor: a 1-year workmanship warranty from OC Flooring, the same on a river-road cabin as on a subdivision two-story. One catch — mills sometimes tie coverage to a minimum pad grade, which is why all three pad grades ride along to the appointment.
